questions.question: What is a Trusted Asset in an AI/BI Genie Space?
options: A table, view, or function that Genie is explicitly allowed to query
Any table in Unity Catalog
A model that has been certified for production
A schema with row-level security
questions.correctAnswer: A table, view, or function that Genie is explicitly allowed to query
questions.explanation: Trusted Assets are an explicit whitelist per Genie Space. Even if a table exists in Unity Catalog, Genie can only see it if it's been added to the Trusted Assets list. This is the governance boundary.

questions.question: When should you write a Genie Instruction?
options: When business users consistently ask the same question and get the wrong answer because of ambiguous column names
Only for metric views
Once when the Genie Space is created, never again
Only when a user reports a bug
questions.correctAnswer: When business users consistently ask the same question and get the wrong answer because of ambiguous column names
questions.explanation: Instructions are for ambiguity that schema metadata can't resolve. Common examples: 'revenue' (gross vs net), 'active user' (DAU vs MAU), 'last quarter' (calendar vs fiscal). You add instructions iteratively as patterns emerge.

questions.question: What's the difference between a Metric View and a regular SQL view?
options: Metric Views are first-class UC objects with structured metric definitions (dimensions, measures, filters); regular views are just saved SQL
Metric Views are slower than regular views
Regular views are deprecated in Unity Catalog
There is no difference
questions.correctAnswer: Metric Views are first-class UC objects with structured metric definitions (dimensions, measures, filters); regular views are just saved SQL
questions.explanation: Metric Views (UC-native) declare dimensions, measures, and filters as structured metadata. Genie understands this structure and can use it for NL→SQL translation. Regular SQL views are opaque to Genie — it has to parse the SQL itself.

questions.question: A user edits a generated SQL answer in Genie. What happens?
options: The edit becomes training signal — Genie is more likely to produce that SQL for similar future questions
Nothing — edits are not stored
The edit is sent to Databricks support
The edit triggers a pipeline re-run
questions.correctAnswer: The edit becomes training signal — Genie is more likely to produce that SQL for similar future questions
questions.explanation: Edits in the Genie feedback loop create a positive training signal. Combined with upvotes on good answers, this is how Genie adapts to your specific data and terminology over time. It's a per-Space tuning loop.

questions.question: [Recall: Unity Catalog] How is row-level access enforced when a user queries through Genie?
options: Genie respects Unity Catalog permissions on the underlying tables; if a user can't SELECT the table directly, they can't see it in Genie
Genie has its own permission system separate from UC
Permissions are bypassed in Genie for self-service
Genie requires admin approval for every query
questions.correctAnswer: Genie respects Unity Catalog permissions on the underlying tables; if a user can't SELECT the table directly, they can't see it in Genie
questions.explanation: Genie is governed by Unity Catalog. Permissions, row filters, and column masks all apply transparently. A user asking 'show me all orders' through Genie sees only the rows their UC permissions allow — same as if they'd written the SQL themselves.

learnings: Trusted Assets are the security boundary for Genie
Instructions disambiguate business terms that schema metadata can't
Metric Views are structured semantic-layer objects Genie prefers
Feedback is a per-Space tuning loop
UC permissions are enforced transparently through Genie
